title: Quiche aux Épinards
subtitle: French spinach and Gruyère tart
excerpt: Quiche aux épinards is a classic French tart of wilted spinach, Gruyère, and a cream and egg custard in a blind-baked shortcrust case. The spinach must be very well drained before it goes into the filling: water from spinach is the main reason this quiche goes wrong.
sourceNotes: Spinach and cheese tarts are found across the French classical repertoire. The combination of épinards (spinach) with Gruyère reflects the Swiss-influenced cooking of the Savoie and Jura regions.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze fully cooled and wrapped. Defrost overnight in the fridge. Reheat at 160°C fan for 15 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Bake the day before. Serve at room temperature or reheated.

content.text: Spinach contains an enormous amount of water. Wilt it, then squeeze it, and squeeze it again. A standard 400 g bag of fresh spinach contains enough water to make the filling wet and the pastry soggy if it is not wrung out properly. The custard: eggs, cream, and Gruyère: is straightforward; getting the spinach dry is the work.

Melt the butter in a large pan over medium heat. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds. Add the spinach in batches and wilt, turning with tongs, until completely wilted. Tip into a colander and leave to cool enough to handle.
Squeeze the spinach with your hands, then roll in a clean tea towel and wring hard to remove all remaining liquid. Chop roughly. The spinach should be almost dry.

Roll the pastry to 3 mm thick and line a 23 cm tart tin. Chill 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Line with baking parchment and baking beans. Blind-bake 15 minutes, remove beans and paper, bake 5 minutes more. Reduce oven to 180°C fan.

Spread the chopped spinach over the base of the pastry case. Scatter over three-quarters of the Gruyère. Whisk the eggs, double cream, salt, pepper, and nutmeg together and pour over the spinach. Top with the remaining Gruyère.
Bake at 180°C fan for 30 to 35 minutes until the custard is just set with a slight wobble in the centre. Rest 10 minutes before unmoulding.

items.symptom: Filling is watery and the pastry base is wet
items.cause: Spinach was not sufficiently dried before going into the filling
items.fix: Squeeze spinach twice: once by hand, once in a tea towel. Fresh baby spinach needs even more wringing than mature leaves.

content.text: Replace the Gruyère with goat's cheese for a sharper, tangier filling. Add a handful of pine nuts for texture. A little lemon zest in the custard brightens the overall flavour.
